questions.context: My landlord promised that he will repair the heater.
questions.instruction: Correct the sentence by rewriting it in full.
questions.correctAnswer: My landlord promised that he would repair the heater.
questions.explanation: After the past verb 'promised', reported speech usually shifts 'will' to 'would', so it's 'he would repair'.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: My landlord promised that he is repair the heater.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: You changed the modal, but 'is' can't be followed by a bare verb here.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: My landlord promised that he will to repair the heater.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: You added 'to' after 'will', but modals take a bare verb and the tense still needs changing.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: My landlord promised that he would to repair the heater.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: You fixed 'would', but a modal is followed by a bare verb, so 'to' is wrong.

questions.context: The flat has a sun in the living room all afternoon.
questions.instruction: Correct the sentence by rewriting it in full.
questions.correctAnswer: The flat has the sun in the living room all afternoon.
questions.explanation: There is only one sun, so it normally takes 'the', as in 'the sun'.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: The flat has sun in the living room all afternoon.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: Dropping the article is tempting, but here we mean the one sun we all know, so it needs 'the'.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: The flat has an sun in the living room all afternoon.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: 'An' comes before vowel sounds, and 'sun' starts with a consonant sound; it also needs 'the'.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: A flat has a sun in the living room all afternoon.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: You changed the wrong article and left 'a sun' unchanged.

questions.context: You are renting a flat. The agent says: "The contract is a legal rule here, so you ___ sign it before you get the keys."
questions.instruction: Fill in the blank with one modal verb.
questions.explanation: 'Must' expresses a strong obligation, which fits a legal requirement before you get the keys.

commonWrongAnswers.comment: 'Might' shows a small possibility, not a legal requirement.
'Could' suggests an option or possibility, but this is an obligation.
'Can' means ability or permission, which is too weak for a legal requirement.

questions.context: We live in this neighbourhood since 2018.
questions.instruction: Correct the sentence by rewriting it in full.
questions.correctAnswer: We have lived in this neighbourhood since 2018.
questions.explanation: With 'since' and a situation continuing until now, we use the present perfect: 'have lived'.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: We lived in this neighbourhood since 2018.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: Past simple suggests the situation is finished, but 'since' links the past to now.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: We are living in this neighbourhood since 2018.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: Present continuous doesn't go with 'since'; use the present perfect.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: We have live in this neighbourhood since 2018.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: You used the right idea, but the present perfect needs 'lived', not 'live'.

questions.context: Our flat is too small, so we are considering ___ to a bigger house next year. (move)
questions.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct form of the verb.
questions.explanation: After 'consider', the next verb takes -ing, so it's 'considering moving'.

commonWrongAnswers.comment: Many verbs take 'to', but after 'consider' you use the -ing form.
The bare verb doesn't fit after 'considering'; you need -ing.
The past form doesn't work after 'considering'; use the -ing form.
